english: I'll prepare the meeting materials.
tip: -(으)ㄹ게요 = I'll (promise): 준비할게요 (junbihalgeyo) = I'll get it ready.

english: I have to submit the report by today.
tip: -아/어야 해요 = have to: 내야 해요 (naeya haeyo) = have to submit it.

english: I sent an email to the manager.
tip: To someone above you, 'to' is 께 (kke), not 한테 (hante): 부장님께 (bujangnimkke) = to the manager. The particle itself carries the respect.

english: I asked the team leader.
tip: 여쭤봤어요 (yeojjwobwasseoyo) is the humble way to ask someone above you – plain 물어보다 (mureoboda) would feel too casual toward a team leader. It pairs naturally with 께 (kke).

english: The meeting took a whole three hours.
tip: -이나 (-ina) after an amount adds surprise at how much: 세 시간이나 (se sigan-ina) = a whole three hours. Without it, 세 시간 (se sigan) is just neutral fact.

english: I go to an academy even on weekends.
tip: -에도 = even at/on: 주말에도 (jumare-do) = even on weekends.

english: The internship experience really helped.
tip: 도움이 됐어요 (doumi dwaesseoyo) is literally 'became a help' – helpful things 'become' in Korean with 되다 (doeda), rather than 'being' helpful.

english: I'm so happy to have gotten my first paycheck.
tip: -아/어서 = and so: 받아서 (badaseo) = got it, and so...

english: I bought my parents their first gift from me.
tip: -아/어 드리다 = do humbly for an elder: 사 드렸어요 (sa deuryeosseoyo).

english: After taxes, the take-home pay is small.
tip: -(으)면 = if/when: 빼면 (ppaemyeon) = if you subtract it.

english: I'll change jobs using my experience.
tip: 살리다 (sallida) means 'bring to life' – and Korean uses it for putting skills to work: 경력을 살려서 (gyeongnyeogeul sallyeoseo) = bringing your experience to life.

english: I've decided to resign next month.
tip: -기로 했어요 = decided to: 퇴사하기로 했어요 (toesahagiro haesseoyo).

english: The manager was quite sorry to see me go.
tip: You can't state someone else's inner feeling bare in Korean – it takes -어하다 (-eohada): 아쉬워하셨어요 (aswiwohasyeosseoyo) = showed regret, not a direct 'was sorry'.

english: It takes a whole hour to get to the office.
tip: -까지 = up to/as far as: 회사까지 (hoesakkaji) = all the way to the office.

english: My parents were really pleased.
tip: 좋다 (jota) states your own feeling; for someone else's liking you need 좋아하다 (joahada): 좋아하셨어요 (joahasyeosseoyo) = they showed they were pleased.

english: I spoke confidently in the interview.
tip: 자신 있게 (jasin itge) = confidently; -게 turns an adjective into an adverb.

english: The new team leader is really nice.
tip: Even adjectives honor their subject: 좋으세요 (joeuseyo) uses the honorific -(으)세요 (-(eu)seyo) ending because it describes 팀장님 (timjangnim). Plain 좋아요 (joayo) would drop the respect.

english: My goal is to become a team leader.
tip: 되는 거예요 (doeneun geoyeyo) wraps the verb as 'the thing of becoming' – Korean needs -는 거 (-neun geo) to let a verb sit after 'my goal is', where English uses 'to become'.

english: It's okay even if you make a mistake.
tip: 실수해도 (silsuhaedo) carries -아/어도 (-a/eodo) = 'even if': 실수해도 괜찮아요 (gwaenchanayo) = it's okay even if you slip up. One ending covers the whole 'even if' clause.

english: I didn't give up and kept applying.
tip: -지 않고 = without doing: 포기하지 않고 (pogihaji anko) = without giving up.

english: It is new work. So I am a little nervous.
tip: Before a noun, an adjective takes -(으)ㄴ (-(eu)n): 새로운 일 (saeroun il) = new work. The dictionary form 새롭다 (saeropda) can't sit in front of a noun as-is.

english: Still, I just need to learn hard.
tip: -(으)면 돼요 = it's enough if / just need to: 배우면 돼요 (baeumyeon dwaeyo).

english: I like working with people.
tip: 일하는 게 (ilhaneun ge) turns 'work' into 'the doing of work' – -는 게 (-neun ge) makes a verb something you can like: 일하는 게 좋아요 (joayo) = I like working.

english: I want to open one more account.
tip: 더 (deo) tacks 'more' onto an amount: 하나 더 (hana deo) = one more. Same pattern for anything extra – 조금 더 (jogeum deo) = a bit more.

english: There's hardly any balance in my account.
tip: 얼마 (eolma) usually asks 'how much?', but before 없다 (eopda) it means 'much of anything': 잔액이 얼마 없어요 (janaegi eolma eopseoyo) = the balance is hardly anything.

english: I forgot my account PIN.
tip: 잊어버렸어요 (ijeobeoryeosseoyo) contains 버리다 (beorida = throw away): tacked onto a verb it means done completely – and often regrettably. Forgot, gone.

english: I check my balance on the app.
tip: -(으)로 = by means of: 앱으로 (aebeuro) = via the app.

english: I withdrew a little cash.
tip: 찾다 (chatda) normally means 'to find', but with money it means withdraw: 현금을 조금 찾았어요 (hyeongeumeul jogeum chajasseoyo) = I withdrew a little cash – you 'find' money at the bank.

english: The bank closes at four.
tip: Clock hours use native numbers: 네 시 (ne si) = four o'clock.

english: I signed up for a three-year savings plan.
tip: -짜리 = one worth/of: 삼 년짜리 (sam nyeonjjari) = a three-year one.
